headline: Stocks post a winning week while yield pressure merely steadies
body: Equities closed out the week on firmer footing: the S&P 500 rose 0.51% Friday to 7,743.41, the Nasdaq Composite added 0.5% to 27,068.72, and the Dow gained 0.93% to 51,828.62, giving the market its first winning week in three (S&P +1.2%, Nasdaq +2%, Dow +0.3%). The advance leaned heavily on renewed buying in AI-related megacaps, while the small-cap Russell 2000 lagged and several sectors — financials and utilities among them — remain down roughly 5% for the month, pointing to narrow rather than broad-based participation. Underneath the rally, bond-market stress has stopped worsening but hasn't reversed: the 10-year Treasury yield held near 5.17%, and the CNN Fear & Greed Index ticked up only modestly to 37, still squarely in Fear territory following the Fed's September 16 hike to 3.75%-4%.

The month's dominant swing factor has been oil, tied to the Strait of Hormuz standoff with Iran: crude retreated toward $93 a barrel Friday on reports of Qatari-mediated talks toward a phased US-Iran deal, easing one strand of the inflation story that had been pushing yields higher. That relief looks provisional rather than settled, with subsequent reporting flagging renewed escalation risk heading into the new week. Meanwhile 30-year mortgage rates near 7.45%, a two-year high, show higher-for-longer financing costs still weighing on the real economy even as risk assets grind higher. Retail-forum trackers didn't surface a dominant single-stock or thematic narrative today, so this read leans more on price action and macro positioning than on social sentiment.
